{"grade": 1, "complete": false, "main_gap": "The central 'finite-transversal / finite blocker' lemma is false as stated for arbitrary pairwise-intersecting families of finite sets, and its König-lemma 'proof' is invalid; the real arithmetic content is thus never proved.", "errors": [{"description": "The 'finite blocker' claim is false. Counterexample: E_i = {a_1,...,a_i,b_i} (i≥1) is pairwise intersecting (all contain a_1), has member {a_1,b_1} of size 2, yet has infinitely many inclusion-minimal finite transversals: {a_1}, {b_1,a_2}, {b_1,b_2,a_3}, .... Hence the lemma, and with it the whole finiteness of b_1,...,b_s, is unproved.", "quote": "If a family of finite sets is pairwise intersecting and has a member $C$ of size $r$, then it has only finitely many inclusion-minimal finite transversals."}, {"description": "The purported proof of the blocker fact is hand-waving: the pruning/contraction rules ('retain only branches which can still be extended', 'contract a node whenever an earlier chosen element has become dispensable') are never made precise, and the König argument silently assumes the contradiction it needs. It cannot be correct since the statement is false.", "quote": "Retain at a node only those branches which can still be extended to an inclusion-minimal finite transversal, and contract a node whenever an earlier chosen element has become dispensable."}, {"description": "The problem's actual difficulty — using the greedy/minimality structure of the sequence (not just pairwise coprimality failure) to show only finitely many minimal prime-blocking sets occur — is entirely bypassed. Only the pairwise-intersecting property of {P(a_i)} is used, which is provably insufficient.", "quote": "We apply the lemma to
\[
 \mathcal F=\{P(a_i):i\ge1\}.
\]"}], "notes": "Correct and cleanly written parts: the sequence is the increasing enumeration of S from a_1 on, and periodicity of S yields a_{n+T}=a_n+L. This reduction is standard and earns minor credit; the substantive finiteness step rests on a false general lemma."}
